A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same negative-eigenvalue LRNN study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original formal-language, group state-tracking, and language-modeling experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds training curves for the previously evaluated 1.3B DeltaNet models in Figure 7.

M1.justification: The eigenvalue-range modifications in Equation 4 and Table 2 are unchanged, as are the implementation listings in Figures 9–11. The new Mamba explanation in Appendix A.2 documents the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same parity and modular-arithmetic tasks, S5 and Z60 scenarios, FineWeb training data, and language-model benchmarks. Figure 7's additional model-size diagnostics introduce no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain their comparator sets: Transformer, mLSTM and sLSTM for formal languages; Mamba, DeltaNet and the full-matrix baseline for group tasks; and the same Transformer++, Mamba, GLA and DeltaNet rows in Table 4.

E3.justification: Figure 7 changes its stated training budget from 32B to 100B tokens, and Figure 3 corrects the smaller DeltaNet caption from 370M to 340M parameters. These are limited reporting corrections: Section 5.3 and Appendix E.3.1 already specified 100B tokens and 340M DeltaNet models in v1. They do not establish retraining.

E4.justification: Figure 7 extends the training-stability analysis to 1.3B DeltaNet, while replacing the smaller models' training-loss and validation diagnostics with smoothed training-perplexity plots. The remaining ablations and length-generalization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain best-of-three results in Table 3, median and median absolute deviation across three seeds in Table 5, and mean with 95% confidence intervals in Figure 4. The three-seed S5 and single-seed Z60 reporting also remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 7 adds 1.3B DeltaNet training-perplexity trajectories and removes the smaller models' validation-loss and validation-perplexity trajectories. Tables 3–5 and the other benchmark plots retain their results; the revision establishes no new benchmark performance gain.

T1.justification: Theorems 1 and 2 drop the eigenvalue-modulus requirement |lambda| >= 1. Appendix B adds an explicit rounding definition and Lemma 1, substantially revising both proofs. Proposition 1 restricts its real-spectrum assertion for nonnegative-eigenvalue GH products to k <= 2, with a replacement proof in Appendix C.1 and revised consequences in Section 4.3.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution 1 replace the headline necessity of complex eigenvalues for counting modulo 3 with necessity of non-triangular matrices; Theorem 2 still concerns complex eigenvalues of products. The parity limitation is explicitly qualified by one forward pass. The main expressivity and empirical contributions remain.

C2.justification: Appendix E.4 newly explains that negative values can make mLSTM normalization terms approach zero. Appendix E.2.1 adds vanishing or exploding states as the mechanism behind full-matrix failures. Appendix A.4 also explicitly characterizes the rounding model as a simplification of practical conversion.

D1.justification: The experiment-code link changes from an anonymous repository to the named GitHub repository automl/unlocking_state_tracking. New Appendix A.2 explains the existing Mamba recurrence and its implemented input term, and Figure 7 discloses 500-step smoothing. Most hyperparameters and the implementation listings are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds focused discussion of continuous-time expressivity, recurrent fast-weight approaches, and nonlinear-RNN parallelization. Section 4.3 connects hybrid GH/diagonal designs to Gated DeltaNet and RWKV-7. The Schlag et al. (2021) reference is also replaced with Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers.

P1.justification: Portions of the abstract, introduction, related work, and theoretical explanations are rewritten, with notation and grammar corrections and a new explanatory Appendix A.2. Author information and acknowledgments change, while the overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 7 is redesigned from six training/validation panels into three training-perplexity plots. Figures 1 and 3 are relocated, Table 4's dataset labels are clarified, and the conference header and author layout change. Most figures and table structures remain intact.

improvement.justification: The central theoretical argument becomes substantially more defensible: v3 removes the extra modulus requirements in Theorems 1–2, restricts Proposition 1's overgeneral real-spectrum claim, and supplies an explicit rounding model and supporting lemma. These address important weaknesses in v1's core arguments while retaining the method and benchmark evidence. Clearer implementation information and larger-model training diagnostics help further. Removing validation curves despite Section 5.3 still citing them is a limited countervailing loss.
